title: P66 (Papyrus Bodmer II): John 16:5-17:1 (pages 116-120)
source: Papyrus Bodmer II (P66), Fondation Martin Bodmer: images from the Bodmer Lab, University of Geneva; Greek from the INTF NTVMR transcription of P66; English from the King James Version
description: John 16:5-17:1 in P66 (Papyrus Bodmer II), the papyrus codex of John copied around 200: pages 116-120, each with its photograph, the Greek transcription and the King James Version.
introduction:
P66 is a papyrus codex of the Gospel of John copied in Egypt around 200, the most complete early copy of John. Most of it is Papyrus Bodmer II in the Fondation Martin Bodmer, Cologny (Geneva); small pieces are in the Chester Beatty Library, Dublin, and the Institut für Altertumskunde, Cologne. The first five quires (John 1:1-14:26) survive as a bound book of numbered pages; later leaves, from John 14:29 to 21:9, are damaged and kept between glass. The scribe made many corrections, some of them his own; only the first hand is shown here.

Each section below is one page: the photograph, the NTVMR diplomatic transcription line by line, and the King James Version of every verse on the page. Pages of the bound book are shown on the photographic plates published by Victor Martin and J. W. B. Barns in 1962 (scanned by the Bodmer Lab), the glass-mounted leaves on colour photographs. Lost: John 6:12-34 (pages 35-38) and parts of chapters 14-21; the transcription ends at 21:9. Where P66 lacks a verse that the KJV has (John 5:4, the account of the adulteress at 7:53-8:11, 16:15), the section says so.

This entry covers pages 116-120 (John 16:5-17:1).
translator_notes: Greek: the NTVMR diplomatic transcription, line by line as on the papyrus. Square brackets enclose letters that are lost or illegible and were supplied by the transcribers; a dot under a letter marks it as uncertain; [...] marks a gap. Nomina sacra and numerals keep the scribe's overline. Spelling is the scribe's (no accents or breathings). Words broken at a line end stay broken as on the papyrus. Corrections are not shown: the text is the first hand.

English: the King James Version (1611), whole verses, for every verse that has text on the page. A verse that begins on one page and ends on the next is given in full on both. The KJV translates a later form of the Greek text, so its wording does not always match the papyrus; material differences (such as verses the papyrus does not have) are noted in the section.

translation.text: <sup>16:5</sup>But now I go my way to him that sent me; and none of you asketh me, Whither goest thou? <sup>6</sup>But because I have said these things unto you, sorrow hath filled your heart. <sup>7</sup>Nevertheless I tell you the truth; It is expedient for you that I go away: for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you; but if I depart, I will send him unto you. <sup>10</sup>Of righteousness, because I go to my Father, and ye see me no more; <sup>11</sup>Of judgment, because the prince of this world is judged. <sup>12</sup>I have yet many things to say unto you, but ye cannot bear them now. <sup>13</sup>Howbeit when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth: for he shall not speak of himself; but whatsoever he shall hear, that shall he speak: and he will shew you things to come.
translation.scan_note: Fondation Martin Bodmer, Papyrus Bodmer II, Bodmer Lab image 1072205287_120 (https://bodmerlab.unige.ch/fr/constellations/papyri/mirador/1072205287), colour photograph of the glass-mounted leaf, shown whole. NTVMR page 1120 (page 116) is linked to this image in NTVMR's page index. 16:5 begins on the previous page; 16:13 continues on the next page. John 16:8-9 fall in the damaged part of the page (lines lost or unreadable), so the English skips them. Checked on the image: the printed caption reads ‹PB II Evangile de Jean, supplément 16, 5-13›.

translation.text: <sup>16:13</sup>Howbeit when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth: for he shall not speak of himself; but whatsoever he shall hear, that shall he speak: and he will shew you things to come. <sup>14</sup>He shall glorify me: for he shall receive of mine, and shall shew it unto you. <sup>16</sup>A little while, and ye shall not see me: and again, a little while, and ye shall see me, because I go to the Father. <sup>17</sup>Then said some of his disciples among themselves, What is this that he saith unto us, A little while, and ye shall not see me: and again, a little while, and ye shall see me: and, Because I go to the Father? <sup>18</sup>They said therefore, What is this that he saith, A little while? we cannot tell what he saith. <sup>19</sup>Now Jesus knew that they were desirous to ask him, and said unto them, Do ye enquire among yourselves of that I said, A little while, and ye shall not see me: and again, a little while, and ye shall see me?

The NTVMR transcription marks this verse as empty at this point of the text, so the English leaves it out. Checked on the image: the printed caption reads ‹PB II Evangile de Jean, supplément 16, 13-19›.

translation.text: <sup>16:20</sup>Verily, verily, I say unto you, That ye shall weep and lament, but the world shall rejoice: and ye shall be sorrowful, but your sorrow shall be turned into joy. <sup>21</sup>A woman when she is in travail hath sorrow, because her hour is come: but as soon as she is delivered of the child, she remembereth no more the anguish, for joy that a man is born into the world. <sup>22</sup>And ye now therefore have sorrow: but I will see you again, and your heart shall rejoice, and your joy no man taketh from you. <sup>23</sup>And in that day ye shall ask me nothing. Verily, verily, I say unto you, Whatsoever ye shall ask the Father in my name, he will give it you.

translation.text: <sup>16:23</sup>And in that day ye shall ask me nothing. Verily, verily, I say unto you, Whatsoever ye shall ask the Father in my name, he will give it you. <sup>24</sup>Hitherto have ye asked nothing in my name: ask, and ye shall receive, that your joy may be full. <sup>25</sup>These things have I spoken unto you in proverbs: but the time cometh, when I shall no more speak unto you in proverbs, but I shall shew you plainly of the Father. <sup>26</sup>At that day ye shall ask in my name: and I say not unto you, that I will pray the Father for you: <sup>27</sup>For the Father himself loveth you, because ye have loved me, and have believed that I came out from God. <sup>28</sup>I came forth from the Father, and am come into the world: again, I leave the world, and go to the Father.

translation.text: <sup>16:29</sup>His disciples said unto him, Lo, now speakest thou plainly, and speakest no proverb. <sup>30</sup>Now are we sure that thou knowest all things, and needest not that any man should ask thee: by this we believe that thou camest forth from God. <sup>31</sup>Jesus answered them, Do ye now believe? <sup>32</sup>Behold, the hour cometh, yea, is now come, that ye shall be scattered, every man to his own, and shall leave me alone: and yet I am not alone, because the Father is with me. <sup>33</sup>These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world. <sup>17:1</sup>These words spake Jesus, and lifted up his eyes to heaven, and said, Father, the hour is come; glorify thy Son, that thy Son also may glorify thee:
